datenschutz.title: Privacy Policy
datenschutz.intro: bewerby processes your application data locally on this device. It can only leave the device through features you trigger yourself, and for syncing between your devices only end-to-end encrypted. This policy describes what data technically arises, where it lives, and what rights you have.
datenschutz.principleTitle: Core principle: local processing, transfer only encrypted
datenschutz.principleBody: Everything you enter into bewerby - job title, company name, contact details, salary expectations, notes, the sender details in your profile, and uploaded PDF files - is stored in your browser's local storage (IndexedDB, the Origin Private File System and localStorage). The bewerby.de server neither receives nor stores this content, not even encrypted. The only exceptions are features you trigger yourself (see below): the contact form transmits exactly the contact details you enter there, and importing a job ad by link transmits exactly that link. If you set up a sync, your content is encrypted before it leaves the device and goes to a storage location you choose, or directly to your other devices; only your devices hold the key. Beyond that, bewerby only connects to load and update the application. There is no automated decision-making, including profiling (Art. 22 GDPR).
datenschutz.storageTitle: Where each kind of data lives
datenschutz.storageIndexedDbDesc: Holds every application record: job title, company, location, link to the ad, contact details, salary expectations, notes, the text of your cover letter, priority, status, tags, dates and reminders, and the history of status changes. Once you set up the encrypted backup, this database also holds a change log of the same data, used to merge the states of several of your devices, and a mapping between the PDF files and their identifiers. If you connect a storage location for syncing, it also holds the access to it (for a folder the reference to it, for a cloud provider the access right), a random id for this device, the progress of syncing, and whether live sync is switched on. The content leaves your device only encrypted, in a backup file or when syncing.
datenschutz.storageOpfsDesc: Holds the binary data of uploaded PDFs: job ads, the stored CV, and optionally a separate CV per application. Each application only references a file name in this store.
datenschutz.storageKeysDesc: Only if you set up the encrypted backup: the encrypted key data, useless without your passphrase or recovery key, and, if you choose “Remember the key on this device”, the key itself. The browser stores it so that it never hands it back out. Neither the passphrase nor the recovery key is stored anywhere. The encrypted key data is also part of every encrypted file, so that the file can be opened on another device with the passphrase or recovery key. bewerby passes on the key itself only when you add a device: encrypted, directly to that device, after you have confirmed the comparison code.
datenschutz.storageLocalDesc: Holds settings and your sender profile: your chosen color theme, chosen language, custom color labels, which cards are collapsed on the board and how it is sorted and filtered, internal markers for which reminders have already been shown, and the sender details you enter in your profile for your cover letters (name, address, email, phone). Those sender details are personal data; like all other content, they leave your device only encrypted, when syncing with your devices.
datenschutz.storageKeyNotifiedDesc: Internal marker for reminders already shown
datenschutz.storageKeyCollapsedDesc: Internal numbers of the cards collapsed on the board
datenschutz.noTrackingTitle: No cookies, no tracking, no third parties
datenschutz.noTrackingBody: bewerby does not embed any analytics or tracking services, sets no cookies, and does not load content from third-party servers. Connections to third parties arise only to a cloud provider you connect yourself for syncing. Fonts are bundled with the application locally instead of being loaded from an external font service.
datenschutz.hostingTitle: Server logs at the hosting provider
datenschutz.hostingBody: When you load this page, the hosting provider's web server processes technically unavoidable access data (e.g. IP address, time of access, requested file), as is standard for any website visit. The logs contain no application data. Besides loading the application, they also record the requests of the features that go through the server and are described below, each without its content. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR; the legitimate interest lies in delivering the application securely and reliably and in fending off attacks. The access logs are rotated daily and deleted after 48 hours at the latest. No visitor statistics are generated; log analysis is switched off in the hosting panel.
datenschutz.hostingProcessing: A data processing agreement under Art. 28 GDPR is in place with netcup GmbH. The servers are located in Germany; no transfer to a third country takes place.
datenschutz.rightsBody: Your application data lives on your device, and you exercise your rights to access, rectification, and erasure directly within the application: applications can be viewed, edited, and individually deleted at any time. Settings also lets you permanently delete all data in one click (right to erasure). The backup page lets you export your applications, PDFs and profile as a file (right to data portability) and import them again. Encrypted files in a folder or with a cloud provider you delete with “Disconnect and delete the files there” or there yourself; when erasing all data you can have the files at the storage location deleted as well. On disconnecting and on erasing all data, bewerby also revokes its access where the provider allows it. Nobody but your devices can read these files. For the data that arises on the server (access logs, contact form inquiries), write to the address below: there you can request access, rectification, erasure and restriction of processing. You can object to processing based on Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR under Art. 21 GDPR. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority (Art. 77 GDPR).
datenschutz.contactFormBody: If you use the contact form, your name, email address, and message are forwarded by email to the controller. This is processed by a script on the same server that serves this page - not by a third party. It is not stored in a database, only delivered by email to a mailbox with the same hosting provider; the data processing agreement with netcup stated above applies. The web server logs the call to the script as described under “Hosting” (IP address, time, requested file, but not the content of your message); these logs, too, are deleted after 48 hours at the latest. The email is deleted once your inquiry has been dealt with, unless statutory retention obligations require otherwise. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interest in responding to your inquiry).
datenschutz.changesBody: This policy will be updated whenever the actual data processing changes. As of October 4, 2026.
datenschutz.storageKeyProfileDesc: Sender details for the cover letter (name, address, email, phone) and the reference to the stored CV
datenschutz.adFetchBody: If you paste a link to a job posting into the application form and choose “Load posting”, that link alone is sent to the bewerby.de server. The server retrieves the posting and returns the extracted text to you. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR: the retrieval happens solely on your explicit request, and the legitimate interest lies in providing you with this feature.
datenschutz.adFetchStorage: The link is not stored, not cached and not logged. It travels in the request body (POST), not in the address bar, so that it does not appear in the web server’s access logs either. Those logs therefore show that the import feature was used, but not which posting was retrieved. The retention period for the access logs themselves is the one stated under “Hosting” above. So that the import cannot be abused as an open proxy (at most 40 fetches per hour), the server keeps your IP address together with a counter in memory for up to one hour; it is never written to disk. The legal basis for this is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR.
datenschutz.adFetchThirdParty: The operator of the retrieved page sees the bewerby server’s IP address, not yours. Compared with opening the link directly in your browser, this discloses less about you to third parties, not more. Your application data – entries, PDFs, profile – is never transmitted; it still does not leave your device. The feature is optional: you can paste the posting text instead, in which case no retrieval happens at all.
datenschutz.syncBody: You can keep your applications in step between your own devices. bewerby encrypts them in your browser with AES-256-GCM for that. The key is derived from your passphrase or lives only on your devices; it is never transmitted. Only encrypted files end up at the storage location, their sizes rounded up to size classes. Their names consist of random ids and the time of upload; they show how many of your devices sync and when, but not what the files contain. PDFs of deleted applications and replaced CVs are removed there on the next sync as well. The bewerby.de server takes no part in syncing and stores none of your application data, not even encrypted.
datenschutz.syncFolderBody: Through a folder: bewerby writes the encrypted files into a folder on your device that you choose. Whether and where they go from there is up to the sync software you use for that folder (for example Nextcloud, iCloud or Proton Drive), and its terms govern that transfer. bewerby itself transmits nothing.
datenschutz.syncDropboxBody: Through Dropbox: if you connect your Dropbox account, your browser sends the encrypted files directly to Dropbox, into an app folder of their own. bewerby only gets access to that app folder, not to your other files. Dropbox processes the files as your contractual partner under the terms of your Dropbox account; in doing so, Dropbox also receives your IP address and the time, name and size of the files. Dropbox may transfer data to the USA; for this, Dropbox is certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, for which an adequacy decision of the European Commission exists. As the files are end-to-end encrypted, Dropbox cannot read their content. You sign in on Dropbox's website. The access right bewerby receives is stored only in your browser's storage (IndexedDB, database “bewerby-db”) and revoked at Dropbox when you disconnect. When you add a device, bewerby passes it on, encrypted and directly, to that device so that it syncs through Dropbox as well. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR; the legitimate interest lies in providing the sync you explicitly requested.
datenschutz.syncOneDriveBody: Through OneDrive: if you connect your Microsoft account, your browser sends the encrypted files directly to Microsoft, into an app folder of their own. bewerby only gets access to that app folder, not to your other files. Microsoft processes the files as your contractual partner under the terms of your Microsoft account; in doing so, Microsoft also receives your IP address and the time, name and size of the files. Microsoft may transfer data to the USA; for this, Microsoft is certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, for which an adequacy decision of the European Commission exists. Microsoft cannot read the files' content. The access right bewerby receives is stored only in your browser and lasts at most 24 hours; after that you sign in again. When you add a device, bewerby passes it on, encrypted and directly, to that device. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR; the legitimate interest lies in providing the sync you explicitly requested.
datenschutz.syncGoogleBody: Through Google Drive: if you connect your Google account, your browser sends the encrypted files directly to Google, into a hidden app folder only bewerby can access. Google processes the files as your contractual partner under the terms of your Google account; in doing so, Google also receives your IP address and the time, name and size of the files. Google may transfer data to the USA; for this, Google is certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, for which an adequacy decision of the European Commission exists. Google cannot read the files' content. Unlike the other providers, Google requires the sign-in code, and later the renewal of the access right, to go through a server holding a secret key. These requests therefore pass through the bewerby.de server (path “/api/oauth/google”): it adds the key, forwards the request to Google and returns the answer to your browser. The single-use sign-in code and the access right pass through the server but are neither stored nor logged. They are sent in the request body, not in the address, so the web server's access logs show only the request with IP address and time. To prevent abuse, the server counts requests per IP address in memory for at most one hour. The access right reaches only the app folder, which holds nothing but encrypted files. When you add a device, bewerby passes it on, encrypted and directly, to that device. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR; the legitimate interest lies in providing the sync you explicitly requested.
datenschutz.syncReturnBody: After you sign in, the provider sends you back to the page “/cloud/callback” on bewerby.de. If bewerby is already loaded on your device, the application answers that page itself, without contacting the server; Microsoft additionally passes the sign-in code in a part of the address browsers never send to a server. Otherwise the request appears in the web server's access logs like any other, including a single-use sign-in code that is worthless without a check value that exists only in your browser. bewerby keeps that check value in your browser's sessionStorage for the duration of the sign-in (key “bewerby-oauth”) and deletes it afterwards.
datenschutz.liveBody: If you add a device by QR code or switch on live sync, your devices set up a direct, encrypted connection to each other (WebRTC). To find each other, they exchange connection data through the bewerby.de server (path “/api/signal”). That data is encrypted with a key only your devices know; the server cannot read it and keeps it for at most two minutes. The requests appear with IP address and time in the web server's access logs; to prevent abuse, the server counts requests per IP address in memory for at most one hour. Your applications themselves then go directly from device to device, not through the server. When you add a device, the existing one also passes the key and, if set up, the access to the storage location to the new device this way, and only after you have confirmed that both devices show the same comparison code. For the direct connection, your devices learn each other's IP addresses. Without further help, devices only find each other on the same network; for connections across networks a STUN server is used once one is set up. Its operator then learns the public IP address of your devices and will be named here. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR; the legitimate interest lies in providing the connection between your devices you explicitly requested.
datenschutz.storageLegalBasis: Everything bewerby keeps on your device - in IndexedDB, the Origin Private File System, localStorage, sessionStorage, and the cache in which the service worker stores the application for offline use - is strictly necessary for a feature you explicitly use (Section 25(2) no. 2 of the German TDDDG); none of it serves tracking. No consent is therefore required for it.

datenschutz.syncWithdrawnBody: A store on the bewerby.de server, offered briefly on October 4, 2026, has been withdrawn. The encrypted files kept there have been deleted, and devices that used it have disconnected from it.

nutzungsbedingungen.title: Terms of Use
nutzungsbedingungen.intro: These terms of use apply to using bewerby. By using the application, you agree to them.
nutzungsbedingungen.scopeBody: bewerby is a free, personal project for managing job application documents. There is no contractual relationship and no entitlement to any particular availability or functionality.
nutzungsbedingungen.serviceBody: bewerby runs in the browser and processes all application data locally on the user's own device; on request it keeps that data in step between the user's own devices, end-to-end encrypted (see the Privacy Policy). It is not a cloud service with user accounts.
nutzungsbedingungen.dataResponsibilityBody: Application data is stored locally in the browser. Without a backup or sync, it is irrecoverably lost if browser data is cleared or a device is changed or fails. Creating your own backups via the Backup page is the user's own responsibility. Encrypted backups and syncs can only be opened with the passphrase the user chose or with the recovery key. If both and every connected device are lost, nobody can recover the data, not even the provider of bewerby. After a key change, only the new passphrase and the new recovery key open what is stored afterwards.
nutzungsbedingungen.availabilityBody: There is no entitlement to continuous availability, error-free operation, or continued development of bewerby. Access may be restricted or discontinued at any time without notice.
nutzungsbedingungen.liabilityBody: Use of bewerby is at your own risk. No liability is assumed for data loss, missed application opportunities, or other damages arising from use of the application, to the extent permitted by law. This does not apply to damages arising from injury to life, body, or health, or damages based on intent or gross negligence.
nutzungsbedingungen.changesBody: These terms of use may be updated if bewerby's scope of features changes. The current version is always available on this page.

landing.headline: Your applications stay on your device.
landing.lead: bewerby is a kanban board for job applications. No account, no tracking, and your entries never leave the device, unless you sync them, encrypted, with your other devices.
landing.step1Body: Title, company, contact. Or hand over the job ad as a PDF, text or link and let bewerby read the fields.
landing.step2Body: Write the cover letter in the editor, take the CV from your settings. Export both as PDF.
landing.step3Body: From draft through sent to offer. You set your own reminders.
landing.dataBody: Entries live in your browser's IndexedDB, attached PDFs in OPFS, your profile in localStorage. Clear your browser data and the applications are gone. That is what the encrypted backup and syncing with your other devices under Backup & Sync are for.
landing.devicesBody: If you want, you take your applications along to phone and laptop, end-to-end encrypted: only your devices hold the key. Without that, everything stays on this device.
landing.devicesPair: Add a device by QR code, without typing a passphrase on it.
landing.devicesSync: Sync live while two devices are open, and through a sync folder even while one of them is closed.
landing.devicesBackup: An encrypted backup as a file, for iCloud or a USB stick, say.
landing.devicesLost: Lost a device? Change the passphrase, and it gets nothing new.
landing.devicesSyncDropbox: Sync live while two devices are open, and through Dropbox or a sync folder even while one of them is closed.

sync.desc: Your devices keep their applications in step, end-to-end encrypted with the key of your encrypted backup. Only encrypted files with random names end up at the storage location.

sync.eraseButton: Disconnect and delete the files there
sync.eraseConfirm: Delete all encrypted files of this vault at the storage location and disconnect? Your data on this device stays. Your other devices still connected to it disconnect as well on their next sync, instead of uploading the data again.
sync.erased: The files at the storage location are deleted, and it is disconnected.
sync.eraseFailed: The files at the storage location could not be deleted; it stays connected. Try again once the storage location can be reached.
sync.erasedElsewhere: The data at the storage location was deleted on one of your other devices. So that it stays deleted, this device no longer syncs there. Your data on this device is unchanged; connect it again if you want to sync once more.
sync.relayWithdrawn: The store on bewerby.de no longer exists, and this device no longer syncs through it. Your data on this device is complete; the encrypted files on the server have been deleted. For your devices to sync while one of them is closed, connect a sync folder or a cloud provider.

pair.addDeviceHint: Connect another device directly to this one, without typing your passphrase there.
pair.title: Add device
pair.scan: Scan the code with the new device's camera, or open this link there:
pair.qrLabel: QR code with the link for connecting
pair.typeCode: Or open bewerby.de/pair on the new device and enter this code:
pair.compare: Does the new device ({peer}) show the same code?
pair.sending: Transferring the key and your applications …
pair.failed: Connecting did not work. Nothing was transferred. Please try again.
pair.privacyNote: The devices only exchange encrypted connection data through bewerby.de. Your applications go directly from device to device.
pair.joinIntro: On your other device, open “Backup & Sync”, choose “Add device” and scan the QR code - or enter the code shown there.
pair.compareGuest: Check that your other device shows the same code, and confirm it there:
pair.joinedDone: Done. This device now uses the same key and keeps in step.
pair.joinFailed: Connecting did not work. Check that “Add device” is still open on the other device, and try again.
pair.liveLabel: Live sync while several devices are open at once
pair.liveHint: Brings changes across between your devices straight away. While it is on, this device checks in with bewerby.de, encrypted, about every 20 seconds so your other devices can find it; like every request, this logs the IP address.
pair.targetShared: The new device syncs through {name} as well.
pair.targetFolder: This device syncs through a folder the new device cannot reach. The two then only sync while both are open; connect the new device to a storage location of its own to keep it up to date otherwise.
pair.targetNone: This device syncs through no storage location. The two devices then sync while both are open. For them to sync while one is closed too, connect both to a sync folder or cloud provider.
